newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica reserves 50 pct shares for retail sales.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica reserves 50 pct shares for retail sales.

text.p: Spanish telecoms operator Telefonica said on Friday that 50 percent of the shares in the state's upcoming sale of its remaining 20.9 percent stake would be reserved for retail investors, local media reported.
Telefonica chairman Juan Villalonga told an unscheduled news conference in Barcelona that the company had presented details of the offer to the National Stock Market Commission earlier.
The total size of the offer, which opens its subscription period on Monday, will be up to 196,738,320 shares or 20.9 percent of Telefonica's share capital.
The size of the initial sale will be 18.2 percent after deducting the shares reserved for the banks backing the offer and to cover a loyalty bonus being offered to retail investors.
Of that package, 58 percent will be placed in Spain with 50 percent or 85,538,400 shares in the retail tranche and eight percent in the domestic institutional tranche.
Within the retail offer, four percent of the shares are being reserved for Telefonica workers, pensioners and pension funds.
The rest of the shares, or 42 percent, will be floated on international markets.

Villalonga, who said the retail tranche would be the key to the success of the sale, said there would be some flexibility in the final distribution of the shares and the small investors could end up with 60 percent of the intial offering.
Telefonica wants to surpass one million shareholders with 10 percent of its clients owning a stake in the firm.
Shares were trading at 3,380 pesetas at 1545 GMT.
